newsitem.title: IRAN: Rafsanjani backers second ex-minister in Iran poll.
newsitem.headline: Rafsanjani backers second ex-minister in Iran poll.

text.p: President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani's moderate backers have thrown their weight behind a former minister as their preferred candidate in Iran's presidential election in May, a newspaper said on Sunday.

Mohammad Khatami, former minister of culture and Islamic guidance, has already been nominated by radical Islamist intellectuals who have moderated many of their views and become political allies of Rafsanjani's centrist backers.
Members of the Servants of Reconstruction group, also known as G6, met on Friday night to formulate their strategy for the May 23 election, the daily Iran News said.

The group comprises central bank governor Mohsen Nourbakhsh, Vice-President for Legal and Parliamentary Affairs Ataollah Mohajerani, Atomic Energy Organisation chief Reza Amrollahi, Tehran mayor Gholamhossein Karbaschi, Vice President for Executive Affairs Mohammad Hashemi and physical education organisation head Mostafa Hashemi Taba.

Iran News said all except Hashemi, who is the president's brother, agreed that all-out support should be given to Khatami, a Moslem cleric who is an adviser to Rafsanjani and head of Iran's national library.
Hashemi wanted the group to have its own candidate, it said.
Rafsanjani's backers allied with other supporters of Khatami and pro-labour forces have been a strong minority faction facing off the conservative majority in parliament.

Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri, conservative speaker of the 270-seat assembly, is identified by Iranian media as the leading candidate to succeed Rafsanjani, who is due to leave office on August 3 and is constitutionally barred from standing in the election after having served two consecutive four-year terms.
Nine men have declared their intention to contest the election. Registration of candidates opens on April 21.
Candidates will be screened by the Guardian Council, a body of lawyers and Shi'ite Moslem clerics which in past elections disqualified all but a handful of those who sought to run.
